fixes.explanation: Close, friend, but kings aren't in this verse. Paul writes, “…the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God.” (1 Corinthians 10:20). Then he adds, “And I do not want you to be participants with demons.” His worry is about the baker taking part in something that belongs to demons.

Jealousy is right, friend. Paul asks, “Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy?” (1 Corinthians 10:22). He asks it right after saying you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too (1 Corinthians 10:21). So the question warns that sharing both tables stirs up the Lord's jealousy. Then he follows with, “Are we stronger than He?”

Mercy is a gentler word, friend, but Paul's question goes somewhere else. He asks, “Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy?” (1 Corinthians 10:22). It comes right after his words about the cup and the table of the Lord and of demons (1 Corinthians 10:21). So he's asking whether they really want to push the Lord by sharing both tables. Then he follows with, “Are we stronger than He?”
